question: How much ventilation do we need during interior painting, and how soon can crews reoccupy the painted rooms?
notes: Retrieval hits the old 09 90 00 revision; expect non-empty superseded_notes demonstrating revision governance.

result.answer:
For interior painting under Section 09 90 00, PART 1 > 1.10 "ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS" states: Comply, at minimum, with manufacturer recommendations for space ventilation during and after installation. Isolate area of application from rest of building when applying high-emission paints or coatings.

1.10.2 "Post-Application": Vacate space for as long as possible after application. Wait a minimum of 48 hours before occupying freshly painted rooms. Maintain one of the following ventilation conditions during the curing period, or for 72 hours after application:
a. Supply 100 percent outside air 24 hours a day.
b. Supply airflow at a rate of 6 air changes per hour, when outside temperatures are between 55°F and 85°F and humidity is between 30 percent and 60 percent.
c. Supply airflow at a rate of 1.5 air changes per hour, when outside air conditions are not within the range stipulated above.

Vacate space for as long as possible after application.  Wait a minimum of 48 hours before occupying freshly painted rooms.  Maintain one of the following ventilation conditions during the curing period, or for 72 hours after application:
a.  Supply 100 percent outside air 24 hours a day.
b.  Supply airflow at a rate of 6 air changes per hour, when outside temperatures are between 13 degrees C 55 degrees F and 29 degrees C 85 degrees F and humidity is between 30 percent and 60 percent.
c.  Supply airflow at a rate of 1.5 air changes per hour, when outside air conditions are not within the range stipulated above.
